## What it is

TAK Server is the server of the Team Awareness Kit (TAK): ATAK on Android, iTAK on iPhone and WinTAK on Windows connect to it to share live positions, markers, chat, missions and data packages as Cursor on Target (CoT) messages. It is a Java 17 program with a PostgreSQL + PostGIS database ([TAK-Product-Center/Server](https://github.com/TAK-Product-Center/Server), README.md).

On OneMind it is an **optional Market app, never part of the base image** (founder, 2026-11-26). OneMind's own native CoT bridge ([#1257](https://github.com/onemindos/ONEMINDOS/issues/1257), design and D-032 in [#1260](https://github.com/onemindos/ONEMINDOS/pull/1260)) carries CoT on the box's NATS bus; this app is for teams that want a full TAK Server next to it, following research W8-R8 (`research-output/09-iot-mesh-offgrid-tak.md`: TAK Server as a container on 16 GB machines, no GPL code in the Apache-2.0 core).

**Licence:** GPL-3.0. `LICENSE.md` is the GNU GPL v3 text; GitHub reports `NOASSERTION` only because of the file name, and the licence-matrix row "TAK Server" [C-LIC-046] records GPL-3.0, so the gate classes it **L2** (copyleft). Whether it is "GPL-3.0-only" or "or later" is UNVERIFIED (no SPDX header says either). OneMind ships it as a **separate program** (an aggregate, GPL-3.0 s5): no TAK code is copied into this repo or linked into OneMind. The image OneMind builds carries the complete corresponding source of the exact release, the licence and the build recipe in `/usr/share/doc/tak-server/` (GPL-3.0 s6). `LICENSE.md` also asks users to review the third-party libraries' licences ("THIRDPARTY.md").

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Image

**There is no public upstream image this app can pin.** Checked 2026-11-26:

- GitHub packages for TAK-Product-Center: none (`gh api orgs/TAK-Product-Center/packages?package_type=container` returns `[]`).
- The Configuration Guide (`src/docs/TAK_Server_Configuration_Guide.pdf`, 5.7, §6.2) says Docker releases are a zip (`takserver-docker-<version>.zip`) downloaded from tak.gov, which needs an account; hardened images are on tak.gov and Iron Bank (Platform One account, §4.1, §6.1).
- Docker Hub has an organisation `takproductcenter` with public `takserver-hardened`, `takserver-hardened-db` and `takserver-ca` images (amd64, tags up to `5.8-RELEASE-103`, 2026-11-16). Nothing in the upstream repo or guide links to it, so **who publishes it is UNVERIFIED** and it is not used. If TAK Product Center confirms it, a later PR can pin it instead (a founder decision).

So the `takserver` container names `ghcr.io/onemindos/tak-server:5.7-RELEASE-14-om1` with an **all-zero placeholder digest**. It cannot be pulled: the app gate fails the pinning check, the tier stays `blocked`, and the gateway refuses to install the app (no passing `scan.json`). Nothing in the gate was weakened.

`build/` is the recipe for OneMind's own image, read from the upstream build files at the pinned commit `5187abd46d82`: `build/Dockerfile` clones exactly tag `5.7-RELEASE-14` (and refuses another commit), runs the README's `./gradlew clean bootWar bootJar shadowJar` and the `:takserver-package:buildDocker` task, and copies the resulting `tak/` folder onto the Java 17 JRE with openssl and Python 3. `build/onemind-tak-start.sh` replaces upstream's `configureInDocker.sh` and runs the Python XML guard before starting TAK. The recipe has **not been run yet**: the next PR builds it on a Linux builder, publishes the image (with its source) and pins the digest here, then the gate decides the tier.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), two containers: `takserver` (UID 1000) and a native sidecar `database` (`postgis/postgis:15-3.7`, UID 999). The upstream README runs `postgis/postgis:15-3.3`; 15-3.7 is the current PostGIS 3 build of PostgreSQL 15 on Debian 13, and PostGIS 3.7 with TAK 5.7 is UNVERIFIED until the first run.
- The database listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so no other pod reaches it, and it still needs the box-generated `DB_PASSWORD`.
- Processes started: config, messaging, API and retention, as upstream's `configureInDocker.sh`. The plugin manager is not started. Java heaps are set from the pod (config 512 MiB, messaging and API 2 GiB each, retention 256 MiB) instead of upstream's `setenv.sh`, which would size them to the host.
- Everything the server writes is on the `tak-server-data` volume at `/data`: certificates in `/data/certs`, `CoreConfig.xml` and `UserAuthenticationFile.xml` in `/data/config`, logs in `/data/logs`. The database is on `tak-server-db`. Both volumes live on the box's `/data` partition (k3s local-path).
- Ports inside the cluster: 8089 (TLS streaming, client certificate), 8443 (web UI and API, client certificate), 8446 (certificate enrolment and user-password sign-in). Not exposed: 8444 federation HTTPS (the first start removes the connector), federation 9000/9001, and the plain-text 8087/8088/8080 inputs (commented out in upstream's Docker `CoreConfig`). Nothing is exposed to the internet.
- Probes: the database with `pg_isready`; TAK with `GET /Marti/api/version` over HTTPS on 8446 (open without a certificate, `ROLE_ANONYMOUS` in `security-context.xml`; a OneMind choice, upstream documents no health endpoint) and a TCP check on 8089. The first start may take 15 minutes.
- Sizing: guide §3.2, "4 processor cores, 8 GB RAM, 40 GB disk storage"; the limits add up to 5 CPU and 8 GiB, the volumes to 40 GiB.
- Backups: `cold`, so TAK Server and PostgreSQL stop while both volumes are copied and the database files and the certificate authority are consistent. Logs are left out. The backup holds the CA private key; OneMind backups are encrypted.

## Certificates

TAK clients prove who they are with client certificates signed by the server's own certificate authority (CA). Here the CA belongs to the owner and stays on the owner's box:

1. On the first start, `onemind-tak-start.sh` runs upstream's `makeRootCa.sh`, `makeCert.sh server takserver` and `makeCert.sh client admin` (guide Appendix B) with the subject fields from the app's settings, and writes the CA, the server keystore and the admin certificate to `/data/certs`.
2. Every keystore and `.p12` file is protected by `CERT_PASSWORD`, which the box generates at install and the gateway keeps sealed, instead of upstream's default `atakatak`.
3. `CoreConfig.xml` is written once from the shipped example, pointing at the new keystores and the local database.
4. Once the API answers, the script registers the admin certificate (`UserManager.jar certmod -A certs/files/admin.pem`, guide §6.2).

## First run

1. Install TAK Server from the Market and approve the install. It installs into `app-tak-server`. Today it is refused, because the image is a placeholder (see "Image").
2. Once a real image is pinned: wait for the pod to be ready (up to 15 minutes on the first start).
3. Until the gateway can hand certificates to the owner, copy the admin certificate at the box: `kubectl -n app-tak-server cp tak-server-<pod>:/data/certs/files/admin.p12 ./admin.p12 -c takserver`, import it into a browser with the `CERT_PASSWORD` from the app's secrets, and open the admin UI through a port-forward of 8443.

## Not done yet

- **A real image** (see "Image"): build `build/`, publish it with its source, pin the digest, let the gate set the tier.
- **LAN access for phones.** `spec.hostPorts` declares 8089 and 8446, but the install sandbox still refuses `hostPort` (contract §12.22, F-05), so phones cannot reach the server yet. TAK's 8443 cannot use host port 8443, which OneMind's gateway holds; it needs another host port. Gateway work, tracked with the CoT bridge plan.
- **Owner-held certificate handling in the gateway:** handing the admin `.p12` and per-device certificates or data packages to the owner (and enrolling phones through 8446) from the dashboard instead of `kubectl`, and showing the CA fingerprint. Rotating `CERT_PASSWORD` is not supported (the keystores keep the first one). Rotating `DB_PASSWORD` is not supported either: PostgreSQL applies `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` only when it first creates the data directory, and `CoreConfig.xml` keeps the password it was first written with, so the two stay consistent only while the secret is unchanged.
- **Where the packaging lives** is a founder call: D-032 (still in review in #1260) and [#1258](https://github.com/onemindos/ONEMINDOS/issues/1258) say TAK Server is "packaged in its own repo" like the Meshtastic bridge (D-024). This directory holds no GPL code (a manifest plus OneMind's own Apache-2.0 Dockerfile and start script that fetch the GPL source at build time), the same as the GPL apps already in `apps/` (Zigbee2MQTT, Paperless-ngx, AdGuard Home). If the recipe should move to its own repo, `build/` moves and the manifest stays.
- **The CoT bridge link:** TAK Server ↔ the OneMind CoT bridge on NATS (`tak.cot.inject`) belongs to the CoT bridge plan, not to this app.
- No web UI through the gateway: TAK's UI needs a client certificate (8443) or HTTPS with a password (8446), which the gateway's app proxy does not front yet. `spec.web` is not set, so the gate's HTTP smoke check is skipped.
- Plugin manager, federation, LDAP and arm64 are not packaged. `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set (the server writes under `/opt/tak`).
- The fixable CRITICAL finding in `gosu` (CVE-2025-68121) blocks `postgis/postgis:15-3.7` at the app gate. The image-build PR must rebuild or repin the database image with the fix, or use another PostGIS-capable image that passes the gate. The same scan found a CRITICAL libxml2 issue without a fix available at the time.
